White Box Unit Testing of the Material Planning 
System
Experiment 4 | English technical report | 22 October 2026
This report tests inventory allocation M33 and purchase quantity rounding M43 in the implemented 
procedural material planning system. The 62 new test cases passed on the recorded source revision. 
Coverage claims below apply only to the stated units and input domain. M33 contains loops, so its 
complete path space is not exhausted by a finite suite.
Table 1.1 Experiment identity
Item Value
Group size 2 members, confirmed by the user
Group and members [Group number] [Member A name and student ID] [Member B name and student ID]
Design basis E3 detailed design, M33 and M43; original E4 experiment guide
Execution Automated local tests; no formal database writes
Status Technical testing draft completed; actual group review and contributions pending
1 Scope and acceptance criteria
The E4 guide requires at least as many selected modules as group members, meaningful complexity, 
all five white-box techniques for each module, and an English report. Two selected modules meet the 
numeric requirement. M33 supplies a five-condition predicate, a nested generator predicate, explicit 
loops, and business invariants. M43 supplies exact arithmetic and three calls to a shared compound 
input guard.
The source files are procedural Python functions. This experiment adds a test harness and report only. 
It does not replace the separate E5 system testing report or establish performance, database, browser, 
or deployment coverage.
2 Measurement method and boundaries
Every case is executed first against the original core.py and then against an in-memory instrumented 
copy of the same parsed syntax tree. The copy records executable statement sites, explicit if outcomes, 
explicit for entry and exhaustion, and actually evaluated Boolean atoms. Its result or exception and 
input immutability must match the original execution. The application file is never rewritten.

Page 2
Table 2.1 Counting rules
Criterion Denominator and interpretation
Statement Executable AST statement sites, including if and for sites; function headers and docstrings 
excluded. A multiline assignment is one site.
Branch True and false outcomes of explicit if decisions plus entry and normal exhaustion of explicit 
for loops. Implicit library, comprehension and exception-dispatch branches are not included.
Condition True and false outcomes of each executed atomic predicate, including the two atoms inside 
the any generator. Skipped atoms count as unobserved.
Condition 
combination
Feasible logical vectors per compound predicate, plus runtime short-circuit traces. Shadow 
evaluations use only safe built-in values; they are explicitly distinguished from executed 
atoms.
Path M43 includes the integer guard and has eight finite control paths in scope. M33 reports 20 
observed traces; no exhaustive percentage is assigned to its unbounded loop paths.
M33 covers core.py lines 30 to 85, including its generator expression. The _integer and _date callees, 
standard library internals, comprehensions and lambdas are opaque at this boundary. M43 covers lines 
90 to 97 and the _integer body at lines 8 to 9. Its 10 statement sites therefore include the two guard 
sites. M33 guard failures are supplementary tests, not a claim of callee coverage.
Tests assume record keys exist and use ordinary built-in values. Missing keys, adversarial Python 
objects, resource exhaustion and all malformed object shapes are outside the denominator. Tuple paths 
are deliberately invalid direct-unit inputs for testing the list-type guard; they are not asserted to be 
JSON input values.
For statement, branch and condition coverage, an exact set-cover search finds a smallest subset within 
the executed candidate suite. These minima do not prove a globally smallest suite across every possible 
input. Combination minima are stated per predicate; the full suite also retains boundary and business￾oracle cases.

3 Inventory allocation design
M33 receives a demand and an available balance. It checks input invariants, allocates at most the 
available stock, distributes that allocation in BOM-path and origin-ID order, and returns new records. 
Neither caller-owned input may change. This control-flow refinement follows the M33 contract in E3.
Figure 3.1 M33 control flow with collapsed helper calls
D1 and D2 are two separate sequential checks in the source; the diagram groups their rejection edges 
for space. Helper exceptions also leave the function immediately. The measured decision IDs and exact 
source expressions are retained in whitebox-e4.json.

The loop-focused suite uses A07 for zero origins and early rejection, A00 for one origin, A04 for two, 
A05 for three, and A16 for rejection after the first valid origin. C02 rejects an empty path, C00 accepts 
a one-member path, A00 visits two valid path members, and A15 visits a valid member followed by an 
invalid one. Zero origins never reaches the allocation loops because the contract rejects it first.
An arbitrary number of origins or path members generates arbitrarily long traces. Therefore neither 20 
observed traces nor the loop cases justify 100 percent path coverage. Full bounded-path coverage is 
also not claimed: the suite samples loop lengths and rejection positions rather than enumerating every 
combination. Finite source-level statement, explicit branch, and atomic-condition obligations are met; 
exhaustive M33 path coverage remains inapplicable without an agreed finite bound and expanded 
enumeration.

7 Purchase rounding design
M43 returns zero for zero shortage. Otherwise it rounds the greater of the shortage and minimum order 
quantity upward to a multiple of the purchase lot. Exact integer arithmetic is required, including above 
the JavaScript safe-integer threshold when the function is called directly in Python. The web input 
limits remain separate.
def round_purchase_qty(remaining_gap, minimum_qty, purchase_multiple):
 _integer(remaining_gap, "remaining_gap")
 _integer(minimum_qty, "minimum_qty")
 _integer(purchase_multiple, "purchase_multiple", 1)
 if remaining_gap == 0:
 return 0
 target = max(remaining_gap, minimum_qty)
 lot_count = (target + purchase_multiple - 1) // purchase_multiple
 return lot_count * purchase_multiple
def _integer(value, name, minimum=0):
 if type(value) is not int or value < minimum:
 raise ValueError(...)
The ellipsis abbreviates the error message only; executed source and exact messages are recorded in 
the evidence file. G1 means type(value) is not int; G2 means value < minimum. The guard decision is 
G1 OR G2. Built-in max is a call, not an invented source if branch.

The numeric-domain combination suite is P00, P01, P11, P14 and P16. It covers all four logical guard 
combinations and both outcomes of Z. Five cases are minimal for these obligations in this suite: two 
normal outcomes and three distinct rejecting guard vectors. G0 to G3 additionally test the shared guard 
directly. For nonnumeric values, G2 may not be defined; short-circuit rejection is the applicable 
obligation, not an invented truth value.
9 Purchase path coverage
Table 9.1 All eight finite M43 paths
Path Witness Control sequence
P-path-1 P00 Three guards accept; Z true; return zero
P-path-2 P01 Three guards accept; Z false; calculate and return
P-path-3 P10 First guard G1 true; reject
P-path-4 P11 First guard G1 false and G2 true; reject
P-path-5 P12 First guard accepts; second guard G1 true; reject
P-path-6 P13 First guard accepts; second guard G1 false and G2 true; reject
P-path-7 P14 First two guards accept; third guard G1 true; reject
P-path-8 P15 First two guards accept; third guard G1 false and G2 true; reject
Each guard has two rejecting short-circuit paths and one accepting path. Any rejection terminates the 
call. After three successful guards, Z has two normal exits. This gives six rejecting paths plus two 
normal paths, all witnessed above. Eight invocations are necessary and sufficient to cover the eight 
complete paths. P16 repeats the first wrong-type path while adding a different logical guard vector.
The path claim abstracts the internals of type, integer comparison, max and Python arithmetic, and 
excludes hostile user-defined objects and resource exhaustion. It is a complete result for the declared 
source control-flow boundary, not all interpreter paths.
10 Validation strength and regressions
All 62 E4 cases passed, including original-versus-instrumented equivalence and unchanged inputs. 
Twelve evidence checks passed. Two existing regression suites were rerun on the same application 
source: 38 of 38 core checks and 114 of 114 planner checks. These counts are separate suites with 
overlapping scenarios, not 214 unique requirements.

12 Findings and remaining limits
The tested units preserve stock bounds and demand quantities, distribute stock deterministically, reject 
inconsistent origins, and compute exact purchase lots under the tested inputs. Full measured statement, 
explicit branch and atomic-condition obligations were achieved in the specified source boundary. 
Logical combination tables explain feasible and infeasible vectors without crediting skipped atoms as 
execution.
M33 cannot receive an exhaustive unbounded-path completion claim. A stricter bounded-path 
requirement would require an agreed maximum number of origins and path members and additional 
enumeration. E5 equivalence classes, boundary-value system scenarios and saved-plan user journeys 
are the next technical deliverable. Database and browser behavior were not rerun in this E4 round.
